pr_title: login: do not issue wall messages on ptys for suspend and hibernate
pr_comments: After looking at this even more, I don't think we should take this approach. As described above, this patch hides the issue, but it makes the logic even more accidental. I think it's fair to say that the logic of using utmp lists for wall messages has severe problems. I think we should revert https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/cdf370626f08ed509a5dde9d5618eed29d625032 instead. I'll submit a PR with a proper justification there.

> I think we should revert [cdf3706](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/cdf370626f08ed509a5dde9d5618eed29d625032) instead. I'll submit a PR with a proper justification there.

Hm, I reverted that single commit but that didn't seem to fix the issue. Still seeing the suspend wall message.
Maybe there is more from that PR that needs to be reverted.

issue_context.title: systemd-login disturbs all ptys on suspend
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 251

**Used distribution**
 > Debian sid

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
 > `Linux debianHome 5.17.0-2-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT Debian 5.17.6-1 (2022-05-14) x86_64 GNU/Linux`

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > amd64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > ptys (e.g. Konsole or tmux) unchanged after suspend

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 >
 ```

Broadcast message from christian@debianHome on tty1 (Wed 2022-05-25 23:49:31 CEST):

The system is going down for suspend NOW!
```
> in every terminal

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 > suspend the system, e.g. on a laptop close and reopen the lid

Please either disable broadcast messages for suspend or add a configuration switch to disable it.

Also reported at https://www.spinics.net/lists/fedora-devel/msg300498.html

Related commit: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/cdf370626f
comments: I join in. It's a madhouse with these constant notifications!
+1 on archlinux

If this was only on shutdown I could understand it. However it is nonsensical and annoying to send these messages every time I suspend or hibernate my laptop by closing the lid. If I close the lid I'm *fully aware* that it is going to be suspended. I in fact *expect* it to suspend. But it messes up my terminals when I get back.
I think it's intended for servers or nfs to advise users of a shared system that it is going down, but they forgot to provide a mean of configuration...
+1 on arch (so annoying)

Also on Arch & some have suggested adding `mesg n` to bash profile.  But it's a no-go for me. Even with `mesg n`, whether on shutdown or sleep, all open terminals are spammed with broadcast messages.

EDIT: Shutdown or Reboot is not really a problem, you can see the broadcast message go through before shutdown but who cares... However, every-time I suspend (ie. close the lid), all my open terminals across all tmux sessions have been spammed with   broadcast messages and this is getting annoying fast.
I believe it's because of this commit https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/cdf370626f08ed509a5dde9d5618eed29d625032

> I believe it's because of this commit [cdf3706](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/cdf370626f08ed509a5dde9d5618eed29d625032)


I don't think. When disabled, the messages remain.

I can confirm that messages remain even when:
1. I set `FarwardToWall=no` in **journald.conf** at **/etc/systemd**.
    I did reload journald service with `systemctl restart systemd-journald.service`. 
2. Use `mesg n` in terminal
In case 1 I've even rebooted my machine and messages still remain.

OS: Arch Linux, kernel 5.17.9-arch1-1
+1 on arch
Could one provide a hotfix solution or would it be required to downgrade to v250 in the meantime in case these wall messages are not desired?
even on shutdown and reboot the message is annoying because it makes the internal speaker beep unnecessarily. And yes, the speaker is needed for other reasons, i can't disable or remove it globally.
What does `utmpdump </var/run/utmp` say? Do you have your local sessions in a terminal emulator listed there?

Reading the linked PR, I am suspicious that this may depend on what terminal emulator one uses. I'm quite old-school about terminal emulators and use `xterm` (for a bunch of reasons that I won't get into). Maybe some terminal emulators update `/var/run/utmp` and some do not?
Maybe its dependent whether one uses [libutempter](https://github.com/altlinux/libutempter)?

> What does utmpdump </var/run/utmp say? Do you have your local sessions in a terminal emulator listed there?

Not in my case, all I see is the X11 logins, ssh logins and reboot records. The kitty terminal emulators do not show up there. Even when I launch other terminal emulators (xterm, konsole) it doesn't happen. Arch Linux with KDE, using zsh for the shell. libutempter is installed by the way. So it is not as easy as just xterm doing this always.
tmux seems to register the ptys for each pane on var/run/utmp as well and that one depends on libutempter too
I don;t know if it is relative. In my system (Archlinux) with 251.1 there is a loud beep each time my system restarts, shuts down or goes to sleep.

The following should work to disable the messages for tools that just call the dbus methods for suspend/reboot etc without changing the wall message state themselves. It's runtime only until next reboot.

     # busctl set-property org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 org.freedesktop.login1.Manager EnableWallMessages b false

As mentioned in https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2129387#c5 , systemd still causes systems to emit a pc speaker beep during reboot/poweroff, but only after a suspend&resume cycle. The fix that applies after a clean boot doesn't persist after suspend&resume and the beeps are unfortunately restored.

I thought this behaviour was intentional, which is why I closed this downstream bug report
https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=1019510

If this is not the case, I'll reopen the downstream bug report as well.
fwiw, after I unmuted "Beep" via alsamixer, I now also get the beeps on suspend as well as reboot.

Hi @ all,

Archlinux and other archlinux based distro users can use downgrade tool from AUR ( yay -S downgrade ; sudo downgrade systemd )  to downgrade last version of systemd from 251 to 250, that solution works for me, shutdown or reboot show me 60 Seconds on window again and beep sound gone.

openSUSE has https://build.opensuse.org/package/view_file/openSUSE:Factory/alsa-utils/01beep.conf in `/usr/share/alsa/init/postinit` due to https://bugzilla.suse.com/show_bug.cgi?id=767270

So the system does not beep by default. Maybe that default should be upstreamed.

I also wonder why those wall messages cause a beep. Does it make any sense to call for attention that way? We could just remove the `\a`  from https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/2164ccdaa21172462d4a6631304591c572b005cb/src/shared/utmp-wtmp.c#L363 I guess.
